entries.8314ae83efa94261: The composition of revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥94,902 million for the domestic business and ¥21,054 million for the overseas business (Vietnam). entries.a515ef9c5da28c7f: A group with ASIA PILE HOLDINGS CORPORATION as its holding company, composed of 22 subsidiaries and 8 associated companies. Its head office is in Chuo-ku, Tokyo, and the number of consolidated employees as of March 31, 2026 was 2,681.
entries.aae51f526cfee71d: Under its Medium-term Management Plan (fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2028), the 'New Five-Year Plan', it sets as its target state 'a leading company representing the foundation construction industry with a high degree of specialization.' Its business strategy is to strengthen the competitiveness of existing businesses by shifting toward large-diameter and large-scale construction, to build a structure for achieving top share in all pile types and developing new market areas, and to pursue technological innovation in Japan and overseas market development. It has also formulated a sustainability strategy that advances measures such as responses to climate change and the realization of workplaces that are easy to work in. Under the holding company structure, it also indicates a policy of expanding its foundation construction business from the domestic market to the ASEAN market.

entries.ede3e28dc0433948: It states that it is the only comprehensive foundation construction company in Japan that handles all pile foundation work, including the manufacture and construction of concrete piles as well as steel pipe piles and cast-in-place piles. It has design and construction departments that are among the industry's leading, and it proposes optimal designs to meet diverse customer needs, and states that it carries out high-quality construction based on its own construction manual. Overseas, it seeks to differentiate itself by leveraging the production capacity and sales capabilities of local partner companies and the foundation construction technology it developed in Japan.
